fundamental.headline: Strong business, fair vs itself, expensive vs peers
fundamental.health: Sales up 83% over the last year, it keeps 42 cents of every sales dollar as free cash, it has more cash than debt.
fundamental.price_text: You're paying about its usual price: its price vs sales is in the middle of its 5-year range. However, it looks cheaper than similar companies once growth is considered. But similar companies as a group are priced near the top of their own 5-year range (their typical price vs sales is higher than 88% of the last 5 years), so "fair" here means fair for an expensive group.
drivers: Sales growth is speeding up compared with six months ago.
Profit margins are widening: it keeps more of each sale than a year ago.
news: Recent AI/infrastructure spending news is news with no clear direction for the company, and it could matter for months.
Recent AI/infrastructure spending news is news with no clear direction for the company; the stock already reacted, so much of it is likely in the price, and it could matter for months.
fundamental.take: Great business at a fair price: a reasonable long-term holding; consider buying gradually rather than all at once. Note: similar companies are all priced near their 5-year highs, so this fair price leaves less room for error than usual. This is research, not personal advice.

deeper.title: What the price assumes
deeper.text: The price assumes about 14% a year growth in free cash flow for 10 years, then 3% (discount rate 9.8% = 10-year Treasury 4.8% + 5%; base: last 12 months of free cash flow). For comparison, sales grew 83% last year; 110%/yr over 3 years — the market expects a slowdown from its recent pace.

deeper.title: Return on capital
deeper.text: 81% (3 years ago 47%, rising) — each $100 invested in the business (debt + equity, net of cash) earns about $81 a year after tax; return on shareholders' equity 84% (3 years ago 38%).

deeper.title: Signed future revenue
deeper.text: Signed but not yet delivered (remaining performance obligations): $3.2B, up 68% from a year ago — about 1% of the last 12 months of sales; customer prepayments not yet earned (deferred revenue): $6.4B, up 215% from a year ago.

deeper.title: Earnings-quality red flags
flags: Receivables (money customers still owe) up 127% vs quarterly sales up 106% (days to collect 54 → 60). Customers may be paying more slowly, or sales were pulled forward.

deeper.title: Multi-year view
deeper.text: Sales grew 110%/yr over 3 years and 69%/yr over 5 years; operating margin today 65% vs a 5-year range of 16–65% (median 56%): near the top of its range (cycle peak risk: margins this high often fall back).
deeper.margin_position: near the top of its range (cycle peak risk: margins this high often fall back)

deeper.title: Cash returned to shareholders
deeper.text: Returned $62.0B to shareholders over the last 12 months ($55.3B buybacks + $6.7B dividends) = 1.4% of the company's market value. Share count down 1.0% from a year ago (buybacks outpacing stock pay).

deeper.title: Analyst estimates
deeper.text: Next year's earnings-per-share estimate $15.92, up 24% in 90 days; 7 analysts raised, 0 cut in 30 days. This year's earnings-per-share estimate $9.31, up 4% in 90 days; 2 analysts raised, 0 cut in 30 days. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

tiles.title: Earnings per share
tiles.sub: +111% vs a year ago · $7.94 over 12 months (GAAP)
tiles.read: Profit per share grew 111% vs sales 106%: profits are outgrowing sales, so margins are widening.
tiles.explain: EPS = profit divided by the number of shares. The quarterly figures are the 'adjusted' EPS analysts track (Yahoo); the 12-month figure is the official GAAP number from SEC filings.

tiles.title: Earnings vs forecasts
tiles.sub: last 8 reports · bars = EPS beat (+) or miss (−) vs the average forecast
tiles.read: Beat forecasts 8 quarters running by about 5%, yet the stock fell after 5 of them: beats are already expected.
tiles.explain: A 'beat' means reported EPS came in above the average analyst forecast. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

tiles.title: Sales growth
tiles.read: Sales up 106% from a year ago and speeding up (from 73% two quarters ago): demand is strengthening.
tiles.explain: Growth of quarterly sales (revenue) compared with the same quarter a year earlier.

tiles.title: Profit margins
tiles.read: Each $100 of sales leaves $65 of operating profit, up from $58 a year ago: profitability is improving.
tiles.explain: Operating margin = operating profit ÷ sales. Gross margin = what's left after the direct cost of the product.

tiles.title: Free cash flow
tiles.read: Only 66% of reported profit became spare cash, usually because of heavy investment; worth watching.
tiles.explain: Free cash flow = cash from operations minus spending on equipment and buildings: money the company could return or reinvest.

tiles.title: Price vs profits (P/E)
tiles.read: You pay 23× last year's profit (its lowest in 5 years; below peers' 97); only 12× next year's forecast, so the market expects profits to jump.
tiles.explain: P/E = share price ÷ earnings per share. Forward P/E uses next year's forecast earnings.

tiles.title: Next earnings
tiles.read: Reports Nov 17; analysts expect EPS of $2.47, up 90% from a year ago. It usually moves about 4% the day after, so expect a swing.
tiles.explain: Consensus = the average analyst forecast (Yahoo, unofficial). The typical move is the average size of the stock's next-day move after its last reports, not an options-implied figure.

tiles.title: Company outlook
tiles.read: No numeric outlook was found in the latest earnings release, so the next report carries more surprise risk.
tiles.explain: Guidance = what management says it expects for the next quarter or year, from its 8-K earnings release.
